clue.text: Quiet, like a spell for recreation

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
as means like, in the sense of similar to
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone hushed, as if under an enchantment, while relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or leisure activity is a form of recreation.

clue.text: Judge appearing in tattered bar attire

indicators.note: tattered clothes are torn to pieces, so these letters are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A magistrate turns up wearing ragged barrister's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattered' rearranges the letters of BAR ATTIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a dispute between parties is to settle it as an arbiter.

clue.text: Cancel the exercise in positive fashion

indicators.note: the exercise is placed in the word for positive, which encloses it

parts.note: positive, as in definite or actual, means real
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Calling off the workout in an upbeat manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' only joins; 'the exercise' looks like a workout cancelled but is school PE, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law officially is to cancel it.

clue.text: Strange individual

definitions.meaning: belonging distinctively to one person, as in a trait particular to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both odd and characteristic of one person alone.

clue.text: He'll make personal representations

parts.note: sounds like a lobbyist making personal pleas, but means someone who depicts persons on canvas

explanation.definitionFit: An artist who paints likenesses of people creates representations of particular persons.

clue.text: Many continually offer inducements, finding only disdain

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
on means continually, as in 'keep on going'
to tempt is to entice with an offer

explanation.surface: Lots of people keep offering bribes and meet only scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn or disdain is the feeling of regarding something as worthless.

clue.text: Reversible uniform

indicators.note: the answer reads identically in both directions, so it may be reversed with no change

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A garment for a team that can be worn either side out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even or flat throughout is uniform.

clue.text: A way to travel up

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A method of journeying upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means mounted, as a rider is up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who is up in the saddle sits with legs on each side of the horse.

clue.text: Darling children's story writer

parts.note: reads as a sweet author for kids, but the Darlings are Wendy, John and Michael, the family in Peter Pan

explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan, whose heroes are the Darling children.

clue.text: Put right about zero-rating direction

parts.note: re means about or concerning
zero-rated goods carry no VAT, value added tax
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Corrected an instruction about goods free of sales tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax; zero-rating means NO VAT is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something to good condition by repair is to put it right.

clue.text: A step taken before conservationists could get clamorous

parts.note: a stride is a step
the NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners go noisy once a first move is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken before' puts STRIDE first; the National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud, harsh and insistent describes a clamorous voice.

clue.text: French pastry for the city retreat

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a lair is an animal's den, a retreat

explanation.surface: A dessert offered as a refuge from the urban bustle.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger-shaped choux bun filled with cream is a well-known French pastry.

clue.text: It wouldn't be fair putting this up

definitions.text: It wouldn't be fair putting this up

parts.words: It wouldn't be fair putting this up
parts.note: sounds like a protest about unfair treatment, but fair means fine weather: you raise this item when it rains

explanation.definitionFit: A rain shade is opened when the weather turns wet rather than fine.

clue.text: Spoilt and troublesome youngster given an outing

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
aired means taken out or exposed, as in airing a dog or an idea

explanation.surface: A spoiled brat is taken out for some fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged or weakened is the sense of spoilt here.

clue.text: Those who want the best are thought heels

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship heels or lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: Perfectionists are considered scoundrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like scoundrels but is the verb for a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamers who pursue perfection aim for the best possible.

clue.text: Honoured companion, a forthright minister

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
plain means frank and forthright

explanation.surface: A decorated associate turns out to be a blunt-speaking churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving a regiment, college or hospital is a kind of minister.

clue.text: Show pine can look quite wrong in a bodega

indicators.note: letters that look quite wrong are jumbled, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A display of pine furniture looks out of place in a Spanish bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can look quite wrong' rearranges SHOW PINE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain a bodega is a wine cellar or a shop selling wine.

clue.text: Till repaired a vessel is no good to one

indicators.note: a thing repaired is put back together, here in a new order

parts.note: an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: A cash register mended, and the pot is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmful act, an unkind deed, does no good to the person it is done to.

clue.text: Head getting in through advocate

indicators.note: the word for head gets into the word for through, which encloses it

parts.note: per means through or by means of
to lead is to head

explanation.surface: A chief makes his way in by means of a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues a case in court is an advocate.

clue.text: A military leader in charge, efficient yet courteous

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: able means competent or efficient

explanation.surface: An army commander in control, capable yet polite.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured behaviour is courteous.

clue.text: Ruined, perhaps, but used to that

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be another arrangement, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Wrecked, maybe, but accustomed to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened by experience means accustomed to something.

clue.text: Learners turning in error

indicators.note: turning means the word for learners is read backwards

parts.note: pupils are learners at school

explanation.surface: Students making a turn into a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless mistake is an error.

clue.text: Coppers turning up late may be seen as a bit of a bloomer

parts.note: p is pence, coins called coppers

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word late is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Police arriving late can look like a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives ETAL from LATE. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Part of a flower's corolla is a bit of a plant in bloom.

clue.text: Having to do with ships in actual use

indicators.note: putting the letters to use means working them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Relating to ships that are currently in service.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime matters concerning sailors and seafaring are naval or marine.

clue.text: Take off from lower ground?

parts.note: sub means under or lower
a tract is an area of land, ground

explanation.surface: Departing from land at a lower level.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to take one number off from another.

clue.text: Certain evergreen trees are a source of food

indicators.note: the run of letters is drawn from within the words, which act as its source

explanation.surface: Some conifers provide nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are a source of' takes the letters from evergrEEN TREEs; 'Certain' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A main course or dish served at a meal is food.

clue.text: Person disposed to adopt the currently favoured policy in credit

parts.note: in means fashionable or currently popular

indicators.note: the policy word sits in the abbreviation for credit, which encloses it

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to follow fashionable policy while in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a leaning or tendency is a person disposed towards something.
